newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: World jurists say Indonesia bars trial observer.
newsitem.headline: World jurists say Indonesia bars trial observer.

text.p: The International Commission of Jurists (ICJ) said on Tuesday that Indonesia had refused entry to an Australian lawyer it had sent to observe political trials under way in the country.

The Geneva-based body, which campaigns for the rule of law and observation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, said the lawyer, Professor Spender Zifcak, had been held at Jakarta airport on Sunday and sent back to Australia.

"This measure taken by the Indonesian government appears to indicate that international scrutiny is now unwelcome, and increases concern about the fairness of the trials of persons who are in opposition to the government," the ICJ said.

A statement from the body called on the Jakarta authorities "to instantly correct this situation and ensure that distinguished international experts are allowed again to observe trials where the Rule of Law and human rights are at stake."
The ICJ said Zifcak, a vice-president of the Australian section of the ICJ, was told he was being barred because of the "political" nature of the investigation he had been asked to undertake.

Founded in 1952, the ICJ is made up of 45 eminent jurists from around the globe in developed and developing countries. Earlier on Tuesday it announced that former U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali had been elected an honorary member.
